summary: 11 files changed or added in a snapshot of tools/audio (git archive of the committed code); nothing copied to the real tree. R1 to R8 repaired with tests that fail before and pass after. No rendered sound changes: P1 173 of 173 wav files read the same loudness and true peak (unrounded), P3 all 75 renderers give the same float and 16-bit samples and the same bytes as the real tree's wav files. One verdict flips in P2: alarm_fuel_low now fails loop-level-swing (84.3 dB against its limit of 80, was 76.3).
baseCommit: the committed tools/audio as of the start of the job; HEAD at the end is c48a037 and the 8 changed source files are identical in it and in the snapshot base

repairs.change: loop_check no longer drops the 100 ms windows under -90 dB. A silent window counts at the floor of -120 dB, so levelSwingDb of a loop that falls silent is 100 dB and more, and the alarm limit swing_max=80 can fail. The number is unchanged for a loop without windows under -90 dB (the test pins 24.4 dB for a seeded loop, the same as before).
testsFailedBefore: listen LoopSwing.test_a_pulse_loop_reads_the_same_wherever_its_edges_fall_on_the_window_grid (read 4.5, 17.2, 9.5, 6.5 by alignment, now above 90 for all four)
repairs.notRepaired: A loop shorter than 0.2 s still returns no levelSwingDb (rules read it as 0.0 = pass), a loop under 0.1 s has no edge fields. Not named in the brief; open.

repairs.change: stereo_stats: a channel with no energy gives corr 0.0 and corrLow 0.0 ('no relation', the rules for two channels fail it) and levelDiffDb is the true difference to the -120 dB floor (about 100 dB; the old code gave 0.0). Two silent channels give corr 0, corrLow 0, levelDiffDb 0, monoRmsDb -120 (the new rule 'silent' catches the file). The fallback of 1.0 for an empty low band of two channels that both have energy is kept. Documented in the docstring.
testsFailedBefore: synth StereoPathRules.test_a_hard_panned_file_fails_all_three_stereo_rules (stereo-correlation, stereo-bass-correlation and stereo-level-diff now all fail; before stereo-level-diff did not)

repairs.change: set_level: info['gainDb'] is the applied gain, info['requestedGainDb'] the requested one (name as in build.py's set_loudness), info['monoSum'] says on which signal the loudness target was measured. The two multiplications that make the samples are untouched. rules.check takes level=<set_level info> and returns a Verdict (a list subclass, so '== []', 'in', JSON work as before) with .hints; a sound with info.limited whose reached level (lufs, or lufsMono when monoSum, or true peak for a peak target) misses the target by more than 0.5 dB gets the hint 'level-missed-by-ceiling: reached X LUFS, table target Y LUFS (stopped by the ceiling)'. Never a failure. build_sound passes the level and puts the hints into checks.hints. build.py process_download: the line 'level[requestedGainDb] = level[gainDb]' is removed (set_level now provides it; it would have overwritten the requested gain with the applied one). The measured applied gain override that follows is kept.
testsFailedBefore: synth LevelHint (7 tests: hint with both numbers, no hint when reached, within 0.5 dB, the half dB limit, peak target, mono sum basis, plain list result)
testsThatPassBeforeAndAfter: tests/test_downloads_build HonestLevel (applied and requested gain of a download)

repairs.change: set_level raises ValueError('silent: ...') in peak mode when the true peak is at or under -200 dB (as LUFS mode already raised) and ValueError('empty: ...') for an empty array; levels.lufs raises ValueError('empty') for an empty array. The set_level threshold is -200 dB on purpose: set_level sees the dry render, whose scale is arbitrary. rules.check has a new rule 'silent' on every path, kind and category: the loudest sample is under -80 dBFS (dither alone reaches about -84 dBFS, the quietest library sound peaks at -44 dBFS); an empty array returns ['silent'] without a crash.
testsFailedBefore: synth LevelInfo.test_silence_has_no_level_in_either_mode (peak mode gave +228 dB gain without an error)
synth SilentSounds.test_dither_only_fails_for_every_path_kind_and_category (6 paths x 3 kinds x 8 categories)

repairs.change: mean_psd: the file is padded with zeros so that every sample lies in the flat part of the window sum, Hann windows of 8192 samples (the whole file where shorter) at 75 % overlap (the squared Hann windows sum to a constant at 75 %, not at 50 %), the mean is removed once for the whole file and the per-segment detrend is off. The band edges, the fields and their meaning are unchanged. Result: an impulse at the first, the middle and the last sample has the same total power (it was 7e-9 / 8e-5 / 3e-40); the shares of x and of x reversed are equal; lowShare/highShare/centroid of the 75 rendered sounds agree with a whole-file FFT of the mono sum with a mean absolute error of 0.0001 / 0.0001 / 0.0 Hz and a largest error of 0.0005 / 0.0053 / 0.35 Hz (before: mean error 0.0278 / 0.0134 / 153.8 Hz).

A file of 1 to 3 samples gives defined values: zero spectrum (shares 0.0, centroid None, no peaks, peakShare 0.0), loop check 'too short'. measure.main reports the empty wav as an ERROR line with 'empty' and returns 1.

repairs.change: _generated_sounds and assemble_manifest take an optional problems list (return types unchanged). Every generated entry that is refused (all reasons: sha256 mismatch, bad or duplicate id, unknown event, incomplete entry), missing on disk, or fails with an exception adds a line; main adds the count to failures, prints 'generated sounds not built: N' and returns 1. The messages are printed as before and the other entries are still built. The download step is not changed (a missing download still gives exit code 0, pinned by a test).
repairs.decision: The brief names three cases; I count every refusal (duplicate id, bad id, unknown event, incomplete entry) as well, because a refused entry is a sound that was not built. Narrow it to the three if you want.

repairs.change: One pass test and one fail test for every all-sounds rule (sample-rate, channels, true-peak with -1.0 boundary, clipped, dc-offset boundary 0.001, onset-late 5 ms, tail-not-silent -60 dB, loop-seam, loop-level-swing, silent) and every category rule (switch-too-long, switch-centroid, alarm-fundamental, alarm-high-energy, sensor-high-energy, radio-band), plus the structure, energy and stereo path rules with their numbers. Loudness against an independent BS.1770-4 implementation in the test (published 48 kHz coefficients, gating): K-weighting 100 Hz against 1 kHz (-1.8 dB difference from the filter), 50 Hz, gating with two bursts with and without silence between them, 1 s of tone in 5 s, the first five channels of a 6-channel file; the same for levels.lufs. True peak: fs/4 at 45 degrees gives truePeak - samplePeak = 3.01 dB, and a 16 kHz sine that a 2x oversampling would miss. One test per band edge (60, 125, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000 Hz) with a tone 20 % under and 25 % over it, lowShare and highShare. Ceiling compared with the number -1.0 written in the test and measured with measure.true_peak; all 75 sounds are loaded and checked (the old test saw 28). Constants and weak assertions of finding 22 replaced: listen stereo test now asserts -0.68 LUFS and the note, rhythm test counts 8 and 4 beeps, png test checks 600x1000 pixels, the CLAP hint test runs build_sound with a fake judge (hint and not failure) instead of reading the source text, StructureRulesTest feeds measure.analyse instead of a made-up dict, the pilot tests call rules.check and the rules.STEREO_* constants instead of their own copies of -1 dB, 0.001, 5 ms, -60 dB, 0.3, 0.9, 1.5 dB.

secondReview.summary: The repairs R1 to R7 do what they say, and no rendered sound changed. All 187 wav files under assets/audio/render read the same loudness and true peak (exact), and set_level gives the same samples for 15 rendered sounds in 86 cases (20 of them limited). 118 mutants of measure.py, rules.py, levels.py and build.py were run. 112 were run first and 4 survived: the alarm band edge, the radio upper edge, the clipped count and the per-segment detrend. I added tests, and the 4 are now killed too, together with 4 new edge mutants and 2 for my own fix. No mutant survives. I found and fixed one defect proven by a failing test: stereo_stats and true_peak still gave an unrelated crash for an empty array. Everything else I found is a note or an open decision. The biggest one: alarm_fuel_low now fails loop-level-swing (84.3 dB against 80), so the full build exits with 1 until the owner decides the limit for the alarm loops. Suites: tools/audio/tests 107 OK, listen 80 OK (was 77), synth 127 OK (was 123), test_screen 47 tests with 1 failure that is not caused by the repairs. Nothing was heard.

4_expected_numbers_of_the_new_tests.method: A separate BS.1770-4 implementation (exp6.py): the K-weighting filters built from the analogue prototype with the bilinear transform and the constants of EBU Tech 3341 (not the coefficients printed in the tests), 400 ms blocks every 100 ms, absolute gate -70, relative gate -10 LU. True peak by 16x FFT interpolation.
4_expected_numbers_of_the_new_tests.anchor: full-scale 997 Hz, one channel, 20 s: -3.010 LKFS (the standard says -3.01). measure.py reads -3.05, the known 0.04 dB (open finding 3, inside the 0.1 dB tolerances).
4_expected_numbers_of_the_new_tests.kWeighting: amplitude 0.5, 4 s: 100 Hz -10.856, 1 kHz -9.024, difference -1.832 (the test takes -1.832 from the same filter; measure -1.820, levels.lufs -1.828). Full scale: 100 Hz -4.835, 1 kHz -3.004, the verifier's -4.83 and -3.00 of finding 18.
4_expected_numbers_of_the_new_tests.gating: two 0.5 s bursts of 1 kHz amplitude 0.5 with 3 s silence between: by hand 10 blocks of weight 1, 1, 0.75, 0.5, 0.25 per burst, mean 0.7, so the gated reading is 10*log10(0.7) = -1.549 dB below the burst without silence. My code: -10.573 and -9.024, difference -1.549. measure.py: -10.61 and -9.07, difference -1.54. Without gating the difference would be about -6 dB.
4_expected_numbers_of_the_new_tests.shortClipTwoChannels: 0.1 s of 300 Hz and 600 Hz sines, amplitude 1, repeated to one block: my value -0.682, the literal -0.68 in test_listen.py.
4_expected_numbers_of_the_new_tests.truePeak: fs/4 sine at 45 degrees: sample peak -3.01 dBFS, 16x true peak 0.000 dBFS, difference 3.01 dB (the signal in the test). 16 kHz at phase 0: sample peak -1.249, true peak 0.000. measure.py reads 0.02 and levels.true_peak_db 0.015 (4x oversampling), inside the 0.1 dB tolerance of the tests.
4_expected_numbers_of_the_new_tests.result: The expected numbers are right. The tests compute them with their own filter code and not from measure.py or levels.py.

faultsOrNotes.what: Wrong sentences: stereo_stats docstring said corrLow is 1.0 where both bass bands are exactly zero; it never is (the filter leaves rounding noise, corrLow of two bass-less channels reads a random 0.07). A comment in loop_check and the README said a falling-silent loop reads 100 dB and more, and 'over 90 dB'. A written 16-bit file has dither in the gap at about -96 dB, so the swing is 96 dB plus the loudest window: 73.5 dB for a 0.1 amplitude tone, 77.8 to 84.3 dB for the alarms.
faultsOrNotes.action: docstring and comment in measure.py corrected by me. The README sentence in tools/audio/README.md (loop swing row) is not in the files of this brief and is left; it should say the swing reads 120 dB (exact zeros) or about 96 dB (dither) plus the level of the loudest window.

faultsOrNotes.what: R1 consequence, a decision for the owner: alarm_fuel_low fails loop-level-swing at 84.3 dB against swing_max 80, so build.py exits with 1 and the real manifest page (not rebuilt) still says pass. alarm_hull_critical (79.1) and alarm_heat (77.8) pass by 0.9 and 2.2 dB only. The 80 dB of the alarm loops was written when the swing could not exceed about 76 dB, so it was never a deliberate number; the alarms have silent gaps by design. The fix is either a higher limit or a rule that says what an alarm gap is. I did not change cat_alarms.py (not in this brief).

R4 judgement call: peak mode raises only at a true peak of -200 dBFS or lower. Noise at 1e-9 (-180 dBFS) is still scaled by +155 dB without an error (the new code raises from 1e-12 down). LUFS mode refuses at the -70 LUFS gate. The rule 'silent' (-80 dBFS) catches such a render afterwards, so the build still fails. A threshold nearer -80 dBFS in set_level would stop it earlier.
R2 note: two stereo channels with no bass at all give a random corrLow (0.07 in my test) and fail stereo-bass-correlation. That was so before and is not changed.

Not named in the brief and not mentioned in the developer's summary: mean_psd no longer takes the mean off per segment (detrend=False).
